segments: Chronography of Bar Hebraeus, page 394. One was Ibn al-Mashtub,
and the other was Qaraqush the eunuch.
This man was a Roman (Greek) by race,
and Saladin had sent him to Africa (Ifriqiya),
and he conquered many cities there,
and he returned and came to Egypt.
And he built the wall there,
which until today is called by his name.
He was also the commander of the Arab forces in Acre.
And when the Franks assessed his value (ransom) at eight thousand dinars, he said:
"For how much did Ibn al-Mashtub ransom himself?" And the Franks said:
"For thirty thousand dinars."
Then Qaraqush said:
"I will also [give] likewise;
for Ibn al-Mashtub shall not give thirty while I give eight."
And the Franks laughed,
and they took from him also thirty thousand dinars.
He has other stories similar to this one.
And one of the poets composed a complete book about Qaraqush,
and after his death, published it.
And after the peace, Saladin went to Beirut,
and Bohemond, the prince of Antioch, came to him.
And Saladin showed him great honors,
and clothed him and the fourteen nobles who were with him in royal robes.
And he gave him half of the revenue of the territory of Antioch,
that which the Arabs had taken.
And Saladin was astonished at the prince,
how without fear and with confidence he had come to him.
And on this account he honored him all the more,
and sent him away in peace.
And from there Saladin went to Damascus.
And the King of England appointed Count Henry, his sister's son, in Acre,
and he himself embarked upon the sea to go to his own country.
And it is said
that he died before he arrived. And in that same year,
which was the year 1503 [of the Greeks], in the city of Iconium,
this man had been formidable, dreaded, and wise,
and had taken many territories from the Greeks.
However, when he grew old,
he divided his territories among his sons,
and remained among them like an indigent person.
And whichever of his sons he went to, he would grow weary of him,
and he would flee to another son.
And when he went to Ghiyath al-Din Kaykhusraw, lord of the city of Buruglu (Borglu),
he received him.
notes: [Variant note:] 1505 of the Greeks: at the end of the month of Ab, Sultan Qilij Arslan died.
